text:
Maya Chen: FYI hitting a weird thing on Windows dev machines — our Node sample app flips to DEBUG logs even when REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info is set in CI.
Trent Lopez: Huh, can you paste the exact env + command you used?
Maya Chen: `SET REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info && node sample-app/index.js`
Maya Chen: But output shows a ton of debug lines from the SDK: `rt:debug` prefixed entries.
Olivia Park: We saw something vaguely similar on win32 a while back — env parsing uses `process.env` with a lowercase key fallback. Might be a case normalization bug?
Samir Gupta: Also check OTEL envs — if OTEL_LOG_LEVEL or OTEL_SAMPLER is unset the OpenTelemetry shim might force debug to help onboarding. Could be auto-config kicking in.
Maya Chen: Confirmed: `process.env.REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL` is present, but the runtime prints: `log level unset, falling back to debug (windows-autoconfig)`
Trent Lopez: Oof. Repro steps for me: node v18.16 on Windows 11, sample-app uses `redwood-logger@0.8.1` and `@redwood/otel-hooks` auto-init.
Trent Lopez: Quick patch I tried: setting `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` AND `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL_FORCE=true` avoids debug. Not ideal.
Olivia Park: Does this interact with the OpenTelemetry hook order? If otel.init runs after logger.init, the logging hook may register a fallback request id generator that logs more info.
Maya Chen: Another symptom: request IDs are being truncated in logs when OTEL is enabled. `X-Request-Id: a1b2c3...` shows `a1b2` only.
Samir Gupta: That matches a known hook-order race — when the log hook attaches before the trace context is ready it writes a placeholder `reqid.short` and later otel replaces full id, but logger earlier redacted it incorrectly.
Trent Lopez: Workaround that worked for me: initialize OpenTelemetry first, then call `require('redwood-logger').init()`; or set `LOG_HOOK_PRIORITY=high` when starting the sample app.
Maya Chen: Can we make the SDK default to not flip to DEBUG on Windows? It breaks CI logs and obscures real issues.
Olivia Park: Agreed. Proposal: 1) stop auto-debug kick-in on win32, 2) ensure logger defers redaction until after otel context resolution, 3) add a one-line onboarding note in sample-app README about init order.
Samir Gupta: I'll open a quick PR: disable the fallback debug auto-config for Windows and add a `logHookPriority` option to the logger constructor.
Trent Lopez: If you add a feature flag env (e.g., `REDWOOD_DISABLE_WIN_AUTOCONFIG=true`) we can revert faster if needed.
devex-bot: PR opened by Samir -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-logger/pull/428 :eyes:
Maya Chen: Thanks! I can validate on a Windows VM tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Olivia Park: Also adding an e2e test that spins up the sample app on a Windows runner would have caught this earlier. Can we schedule that in the infra backlog?
Samir Gupta: Yup, adding ticket INFRA-882.
Maya Chen: Great — that should unblock our onboarding checklist.
Trent Lopez: Nice teamwork.
